identity.title: The solar chromosphere at millimetre and ultraviolet wavelengths. I. Radiation temperatures and a detailed comparison

paper_type_evidence.quote: This study is primarily based on observations of the solar active region AR 12470 by ALMA on 18 December 2015.

evidence.quote: The field of view (FOV) includes the leading sunspot of the active region AR 12470 surrounded by plages and quasi-quiet[^1] areas, close to the solar disc-center (with cosine of heliocentric angle $\approx0.97$).

question.value: How do chromospheric radiation temperatures from ALMA Band 6 (1.3 mm) compare with those from IRIS UV lines in regions of different magnetic field strength?

evidence.quote: The present work provides distributions of the radiation temperature at various chromospheric heights sampled by the ALMA 1.3 mm passband and the IRIS observations at near- and far-UV wavelengths
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00020.SV.
was obtained in ALMA band 6 (centred at 239 GHz; 1.25 mm) on 18 December 2015

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: Four spectral windows of 2 GHz each, 128 channels each (TDM); SW0-SW3 at 1.303, 1.292, 1.219, 1.209 mm (230, 232, 246, 248 GHz)

evidence.quote: Four spectral windows (sub bands), with a bandwidth of 2 GHz each, were recorded. Each spectral window (SW) includes 128 channels

arrays.value: Twenty-one 12 m and nine 7 m antennas plus total-power array

evidence.quote: The data was taken using a heterogeneous array configuration consisting of twenty-one 12 m and nine 7 m antennas.

angular_resolution.value: Beam about 2.2'' x 0.7'' (Gaussian kernel equivalent to the ALMA PSF)

evidence.quote: equivalent to a $2.2\ensuremath{''}\times0.7\ensuremath{''}$ Gaussian kernel
an integration time of 6.048 s for each point
on 18 December 2015 between 19:39:25–20:02:34 UT

provided.value: Near/far-UV spectra (Mg II h/k, C II, O I, Si IV) in a 320-step raster

evidence.quote: The ALMA observations were supported by the IRIS spacecraft in the “very large dense 320-step raster” mode with 2 s exposure time per step.

provided.value: Co-alignment images and HMI VFISV field strength maps for region masks

evidence.quote: We also use the results of the Milne-Eddington Stokes inversion of the HMI data with the VFISV code (cite: Borrero2011) to obtain the photospheric magnetic field strength.

pipeline_or_manual.value: Optimised standard pipeline (SoAP) with sub-bands and channels separated; CASA calibration, imaging, feathering with TP maps

evidence.quote: We have optimised the standard reduction pipeline by tuning various parameters, also separating the sub-bands and the spectral channels
is the brightness temperature (with an uncertainty in the order of 5%)
with a sampling resolution of $\approx0.15$ arcsec/pixel

array_combination.value: Interferometric data feathered with total-power maps for absolute brightness temperature

evidence.quote: The TP maps are used to derive absolute brightness temperatures for the interferometric data

what.value: CASA calibration, imaging and feathering steps for solar ALMA data

evidence.quote: included standard CASA calibrations, imaging, and feathering steps (see (cite: Shimojo2017) for details)
The first version of this Solar ALMA Pipeline (SoAP) will be described in a forthcoming publication (cite: Szydlarski2018).

unstated_but_needed: Exact IRIS observation ID and file names

analysis_steps.goal: Derive ALMA sub-band brightness temperature maps

method.value: Pipeline reduction per spectral window, feathered with TP maps; brightness temperature used directly

evidence.quote: Thus, it directly enters our analysis with no further processing.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute IRIS line features and radiation temperatures

method.value: Gaussian fits with MOSiC; intensity from radiometric calibration converted via inverse Planck function

evidence.quote: We calculate the near- and far-UV radiation temperature $T_{rad}$ in the solar chromosphere at a given wavelength $\lambda$ by solving the Planck function

fitting.value: Single then multiple Gaussians, reduced chi-square

evidence.quote: The goodness of the fits at each step is evaluated by means of reduced chi-square statistics

method.value: HMI VFISV field strength thresholds: umbra B≥2 kG, sunspot+pores B≥0.8 kG, penumbra 0.8–2 kG, plage 0.2–0.8 kG, quasi-quiet B<0.1 kG

evidence.quote: 0.8 kG$>B\geq0.2$ kG defining the plage areas, and $B<0.1$ kG to represent the quasi-quiet regions

analysis_steps.goal: Compare Trad distributions and pixel-to-pixel relations

method.value: Histograms per region; IRIS convolved with ALMA PSF, resampled, pixels limited to max 2 min (and 0.5 min) time difference; Pearson r, Spearman rho, linear slope, K-S test

evidence.quote: we only include pixels, from either of the first two IRIS scans, which have a maximum observing-time difference of two minutes

assumptions.value: ALMA brightness temperature represents gas temperature (LTE, Rayleigh-Jeans)

evidence.quote: the temperature can be simply measured under the assumption of local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE)
Furthermore, the linear regression coefficient of the linear fit $m$, which measures the steepness of a linear relationship, is calculated.

validation.value: Repeated with 0.5 min maximum time difference

evidence.quote: we also repeated the analyses with a maximum time difference of 0.5 min
included standard CASA calibrations, imaging, and feathering steps
The first version of this Solar ALMA Pipeline (SoAP) will be described in a forthcoming publication
are computed with the MOSiC analysis tool (cite: Rezaei2017)

used_for.value: HMI Milne-Eddington inversion for field strength

evidence.quote: Milne-Eddington Stokes inversion of the HMI data with the VFISV code

results_numeric.quantity: ALMA 1.3 mm mean brightness temperature, entire FOV

evidence.quote: varies between 4.6–8.1 kK in the entire FOV with an average and standard variation of 6.6 kK and 0.5 kK
Its mean value is the smallest in the umbra ($5.6\pm0.4$ kK
is the largest in the plage region ($7.0\pm0.4$ kK)

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of FOV with time difference ≤2 min

evidence.quote: this selection limits us to only 28% of the entire FOV

findings_qualitative.value: Splitting ALMA sub-bands resolves finer structures than averaging

evidence.quote: spectral splitting of the ALMA observations in a particular Band (here, in Band 6) results in a slightly higher spatial resolution.

claims.hypothesis: Do ALMA Band 6 and IRIS Trad agree?
claims.experiment: Compared histograms and K-S tests in magnetic regions
claims.result: C II agrees best with ALMA (mean 6.6 kK each in the FOV); Mg II is lower (about 5.2–5.6 kK)
claims.finding: Only C II is compatible with ALMA; Mg II radiation temperatures are lower, likely due to non-LTE

evidence.quote: is, on average, compatible with that retrieved from the line core of the C ii, with an exception in the umbra

claims.hypothesis: Are UV and mm temperatures correlated pixel to pixel?
claims.experiment: Scatter plots with Pearson/Spearman for pixels within 2 min and 0.5 min
claims.result: Moderate-to-good positive correlations (0.5<r<0.9) except in umbra
claims.finding: UV and ALMA temperature variations are similar spatially, with offsets from the y=x line

evidence.quote: show a moderate-to-good positive linear correlation (i.e. $0.5 < r < 0.9$)

limitations_admitted.value: Time differences between ALMA and IRIS and few umbra pixels limit the comparison

evidence.quote: could partly be due to a large uncertainty introduced by the very few data points entering the analysis

referee_caveats_inferred: The 5% ALMA calibration uncertainty is not derived
Non-LTE Trad vs gas temperature offsets are not modelled
Different formation heights are not quantified
